We started seeing a spike in 5xx and queued requests hitting our reserved throughput at ~09:00 PT. A bunch of our user-facing jobs started failing (500/503) and latency jumped from ~120ms to 1.6s. We have an active rollout that increased QPS by about 30% this morning but we didn't expect this level of headroom exhaustion.

I attached a short screenshot from our edge traces and sample request ids. Can Redwood temporarily allow burst capacity or a fallback model to keep the surface stable while we throttle on our side? We're on a committed reserved pool (monthly) and need this stabilized quickly.

—Luke

From: david_kim@redwood.ai

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-05T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden queueing / 503s right at 09:00 PT

Marissa — quick triage notes:
- Serving telemetry shows dedicated pool headroom drop from 23% to ~4% between 08:55–09:05 PT.
- Tail latency and 503s correlate with a burst of long-context batch jobs from ClearStream's canary rollout (pattern: sustained 10–15s generation windows).
- CPU utilization on the serving nodes is at 86%, NVLink traffic spike, but memory/KV cache miss rate also increased (their workload touches long-context KV).

Proposed immediate mitigations:
1) Enable soft-fallback routing to a quantized model variant for 20% of traffic (preserves correctness for many payloads) — low risk.
2) Offer a 90-minute emergency burst from our shared overflow pool (we need commercial sign-off). Estimated incremental cost for that window: ~$6.1k.
3) Rate-limit large contexts at the API layer for new user sessions (customer-side throttle) — recommend they deploy ASAP.

I'll prepare a one-slide RCA and the exact telemetry for the exec briefing.

—David
David Kim
Site Reliability Engineering — Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-05T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Request: emergency overflow authorization + customer goodwill credit

Vivek — ClearStream is experiencing significant user impact due to a sudden QPS surge tied to an internal rollout. Engineering recommends:
- Approve a 90-minute emergency overflow allocation from shared capacity (estimated incremental cost ~$6.1k).
- Approve a one-week goodwill credit of 15% on their next invoice to cover the customer ops impact — suggested concession to protect the renewal (deal id DEAL-4821).

Why now: their production errors are visible to their customers; they are at risk of pausing the rollout and escalating externally. Ben is on the call with them and pushing for a quick customer-stabilization path. If you approve, finance and billing will prepare the credit memo; infra will apply the overflow and route fallback traffic.

Options if declined: we can provide fallback-only mitigations (quantized variant + customer throttles) but that may not fully eliminate 5xx during peak.

Requesting a short yes/no (or counter) so we can communicate within the hour.

—Marissa
